_note: N4b side content: all pieces with hook, twist, systems, place, leads, acts, reward, mobile note and rank. Full mission-format specs exist for the 5 slice candidates (content/side/<id>.json). The rest are specced to this level; full specs are N4b part 2.

pieces.title: The Pigeon Commodore
pieces.where: Rooftop coop over W 29th St & 7th Ave; rooftops across the Fur District
pieces.hook: Old Ignatz Halloran races pigeons from a tar-roof coop and swears someone is stealing his champions mid-race.
pieces.twist: Rooftop pursuit by sight: follow a bird's flight line across roofs, fire escapes and stairwells (enterable buildings), photograph its leg band to prove which roof it landed on. In Act 3 his birds carry a message for the march.
pieces.reward: $20 a race; the final race unlocks a pigeon-post messenger that shows the next story marker
pieces.mobile: Following is by viewpoint, not aim. Birds pause on landmarks. Every roof route has a stairwell exit.

pieces.title: Night Rate: Stunt Driver
pieces.where: The NIGHT RATE shoot at W 41st St & the west edge (boundaries.json)
pieces.hook: The film's stunt driver quit. The first A.D. bullhorns at anyone who looks like they can drive.
pieces.twist: Takes are judged by the director's shot list (hit the mark, skid on cue, miss the camera car). On take 3 a real police car joins the 'chase' and the witness system can't tell film from crime.
pieces.reward: $50 a take; a crew jacket (outfit) and the director's thanks in the Act 3 wrap party
pieces.mobile: Takes are 60–90 s with generous marks. Retakes are free. No precision steering at walking-speed sections.

pieces.title: The Night Desk at the Ticker
pieces.where: The Daily Ticker midtown bureau, W 26th St & 7th Ave
pieces.hook: The tabloid's night photo editor buys prints by the hour, more if you're first.
pieces.twist: Race the police radio: dispatch lines (barks.police_radio) are the clue. Get there before the press car, frame the shot before the cops tape it off. Never the dead, never victims' faces (content rule).
pieces.reward: $10–75 a print; first-on-scene bonus; a press-pass outfit that lowers witness heat at scenes
pieces.mobile: Auto-framing; the 'first' timer is generous and shown on the HUD. Missing it pays less, never fails.

pieces.title: Hack: Call Your Turns
pieces.where: Penn Station cab line; anywhere in the core
pieces.hook: Cab fares, where the passenger calls the turns the 1974 way.
pieces.twist: No GPS: each fare talks you there ('left on Thirty-Fourth, then down Seventh'). Ladder: licensed hack in Act 2 (Maureen Kehoe), rush-hour fares, then regulars with their own little arcs.
pieces.reward: $3–7 a fare + tips (route-knowledge bonus); regulars pay double
pieces.mobile: Turns are called 6+ seconds early and repeated on the HUD as text. Wrong turns cost tips, never fail.

pieces.title: Hollis's Postcards
pieces.where: Pawnshops, fences, the Corwin, Earl's stand, the Royal (20 hidden across the core)
pieces.hook: Walter Hollis mailed himself a postcard from every port he ever reached. Over the years they ended up all over the district.
pieces.twist: Each card is a short scene (the port, the year, one sentence of his voice). After Hollis dies (M19), bringing them to Odessa builds a lobby memorial wall, and the last card answers what he meant by 'shipmate'.
pieces.reward: A memorial in the Corwin lobby; Odessa +1 per five cards; the last card unlocks Hollis's radio station preset
pieces.mobile: Cards glint at close range; an 'ask around' prompt points to the right block.

pieces.title: Mrs. Cho's Late Husband
pieces.where: The Velvet Moon and the Deuce's 24-hour cinemas
pieces.hook: A widow insists her husband, ten years dead, is alive. She saw him last night at a triple feature on 42nd St.
pieces.twist: He's a bit-part actor in an old crime picture still playing the grindhouses. Track which cinema shows which reel by the marquees (street_text), get the projectionist to run the scene, and give her one more evening.
pieces.reward: Her late husband's watch (sell or keep); the Velvet Moon midnight screening unlocked
pieces.mobile: No timers; marquees are readable from the sidewalk.

pieces.title: The Man Who Sells the Weather
pieces.hook: A street prophet with a barometer and a sandwich board predicts brownouts and is right twice.
pieces.twist: His readings become a free-roam forecast: bring him readings from three rooftop gauges and he tells you which blocks go dark next brownout (lets you prepare).
pieces.reward: Brownout warnings on the minimap; a barometer prop for a lead's home

pieces.title: Four Pianos
pieces.where: Walk-ups across the core; the Varelas apartment
pieces.hook: Two brothers move pianos up tenement stairs for a living, and they're one man short and one rope old.
pieces.twist: A physics-and-timing job on real stairwells: rope, landings, the piano swinging toward a window. The fourth piano is Nick's, sold in his Act 3 decline (if he sells).
pieces.reward: $25 a piano; the brothers become muscle Nick can hire
pieces.mobile: One held button with a rhythm prompt; generous timing.

pieces.title: The Last Telegrams
pieces.where: A telegraph office on W 34th St (invented); deliveries across the core
pieces.hook: Telegraph messengers are a dying trade. The office needs someone fast, on foot or bike.
pieces.twist: Each telegram is a tiny story you see delivered (a death, a birth, a winning number). Choose whether to deliver bad news before or after the recipient's shift.
pieces.reward: $2–4 a telegram + tips; a 'messenger' outfit that makes you invisible to witnesses
pieces.mobile: No timers except a soft 'before 6 p.m.'.

pieces.title: The Runaway from the Garden
pieces.where: Madison Square Garden / Penn Station / Seventh Ave
pieces.hook: During the summer horse show at the Garden (invented), a horse gets loose and trots down Seventh Avenue.
pieces.twist: Herd, don't chase: crowds and traffic spook it. Use the 1974 one-ways to get ahead and calm it with sugar from a diner.
pieces.reward: $40 from the stable; a Garden ticket stub (fight-card access)
pieces.mobile: Slow pursuit; the horse waits at corners.

pieces.title: Garment Rush: Racks and Gridlock
pieces.hook: Pushboys need extra hands, and the trucks won't move.
pieces.twist: Rack-pushing time trials through gridlock, with the hills (terrain on) turning a rack into a runaway. The routes thin out as shops move south in Act 3.
pieces.reward: $15 a run; a speed ladder unlocks Dwayne's sketches being seen

pieces.title: Bulldog Edition: The Scoop
pieces.hook: Deliver the bulldog edition before the rival paper's truck.
pieces.twist: The front page (newspapers.json) changes weekly, and some weeks you deliver news you made. Beat the rival truck to six stands with one-ways and short cuts.

pieces.title: Abend's Board of Skips
pieces.where: Abend Bail Bonds, W 31st St & 8th Ave
pieces.hook: A wall of mugshots, each with a story and a bail amount.
pieces.twist: Every skip has a personality and a weakness (a mother's birthday, a pool habit, a fear of pigeons). Find them by asking around, bring them in breathing. Non-lethal only.
pieces.mobile: Investigation by talking; takedowns on soft lock.

pieces.title: The Dukes' Weekly List
pieces.where: The Dyer Avenue Dukes' garage, W 36th St & 9th Ave
pieces.hook: A weekly list of wanted cars, chalked on a board.
pieces.twist: Car theft through Gameplay's systems: witnesses, call boxes, descriptions. The twist is choosing whose car: a slumlord's sedan earns respect, a cabbie's livelihood earns enemies.
pieces.mobile: No precision driving; the garage door is a big target.

pieces.title: Teddy's Keys: Call-Outs
pieces.hook: Locked out, locked in, locked up: the hardware store sends Teddy.
pieces.twist: Every call-out is a door with a story behind it (a dead man's flat, a runaway's room (adult), a safe that holds love letters). Teddy's 'Keys' skill opens; his ex-cop eye notices what's wrong.
pieces.reward: $10–25 a call; one call-out each act feeds a main-story clue
pieces.mobile: Lockpicking is a held button with a rhythm, no precision.

pieces.title: Fight Night at the Garden
pieces.hook: The promoter needs a door man, and Nick likes a ringside bet.
pieces.twist: Teddy works the door (spot the fake tickets, eject the drunk, non-lethal). Nick bets on invented fighters whose records are in the paper (newspapers.json).

pieces.title: Earl's Runner
pieces.hook: Runner pay, and the street number: the last three digits of the track handle in the paper.
pieces.twist: Pick up slips before noon past plainclothes who know what you're carrying. Ladder: Earl trusts you with the bank on Fridays.

pieces.title: Murray Hill Wagers
pieces.where: Races within the core: Madison Ave hills, the 34th St two-way, Fifth's downhill
pieces.hook: Cabbies bet Nick's sedan can't beat them, on a small map.
pieces.twist: Short sprints that use the real relief (terrain on) and the 1974 one-ways. Wrong-way driving forfeits. Each race is a block-scale puzzle, not distance.
pieces.mobile: Route choice wins, not reflexes; no rubber-banding.

pieces.title: Corner Pocket
pieces.where: Corner Pocket Billiards, over a W 41st St storefront (invented)
pieces.hook: A pool hall where the regulars hustle each other.
pieces.twist: Read the hustler (Delphine's tells), or be the hustler (Nick's money). Pool itself is a simple aim-assisted shot game.

pieces.title: The Teletrack Tip
pieces.hook: Cab fares and barflies whisper tips on invented races.
pieces.twist: Cross-system: tips overheard in cab fares, bar barks and the subway grates. Bet on them at the Teletrack. Some tips are fixes, and Wurtz's unit knows which.

pieces.title: Marty's Want List
pieces.where: Marty the fence, W 39th St & 9th Ave
pieces.hook: A fence with weekly wants: a radio, a fur (!), a camera.
pieces.twist: Find the wanted item in the world (pawnshops, shops, burglaries via Gameplay), or tip off the owner instead and get a reward.

pieces.title: Own a Business
pieces.hook: Buy Hanyang House's half share, the Royal, the arcade, the hardware store, or a Ninth Avenue garage.
pieces.twist: Weekly income plus 'trouble' events (a health inspector's tip, Lonnie's crew, a skimming night manager) that come as short side jobs.
pieces.mobile: Trouble events are short and skippable (income dips).

pieces.title: Hydrant War
pieces.where: Any hot afternoon, side streets near 9th Ave
pieces.hook: Kids (ambient) have opened a hydrant; a cop wants it shut; the block wants it open.
pieces.twist: Choose: fit a spray cap (a block party breaks out), shut it (the cop owes you), or bribe the cop to look away. No danger to children (content rule).
pieces.reward: Relationship and reputation on the block

pieces.title: Snatch on Thirty-Fourth
pieces.hook: A purse thief bolts through the shoppers.
pieces.twist: Chase through the department store's two doors. Being seen helping lowers your own heat with witnesses (positive witness system).

pieces.title: Between Floors
pieces.where: Office buildings on Fifth Ave during brownouts
pieces.hook: A brownout traps people in an elevator.
pieces.twist: Use keys and stairwells to reach the machine room, crank the car down by hand (timing prompt), and meet who was inside (sometimes Lisle's secretary).

pieces.title: Pennington, Fast
pieces.hook: A woman in labour (adult) flags you down.
pieces.twist: Drive to the hospital on the one-ways with her calling the turns between breaths. Potholes hurt; the hills help.
pieces.reward: A name you choose for the baby (it appears in the epilogue paper's birth notices)

pieces.title: Three-Card Monte
pieces.hook: A cardboard-box monte game with a crowd.
pieces.twist: Spot the shills (Read the Room tells), win once, or bust it and anger the crew. Delphine reads it instantly; Nick loses on purpose to buy information.

pieces.title: Tar Beach Thief
pieces.hook: Someone stole a radio off a tar beach while its owner sunbathed.
pieces.twist: A rooftop chase across parapets and over planks between buildings; the thief drops into a stairwell (enterable).

pieces.title: Which Way's Up?
pieces.hook: A family from Ohio with a folded map.
pieces.twist: Reverse no-GPS: you give the directions as choices ('two blocks up, west side of Seventh'), and they walk it. Wrong directions show up later in the paper as a funny letter.

pieces.title: Break It Up
pieces.hook: Two men fight over a bench at dusk.
pieces.twist: Non-lethal takedowns, or talk them down, or let them fight and pick a winner (betting crowd).

pieces.title: Runaway Rack
pieces.hook: A loaded garment rack gets loose on the slope.
pieces.twist: Catch it before the intersection; use parked trucks as brakes.
pieces.reward: A thank-you from the shop (a free suit)

pieces.title: The Three A.M. Phone
pieces.hook: A payphone rings at 3 a.m. every night. Nobody else will answer it.
pieces.twist: An anonymous caller feeds tips about the syndicate, each checkable (a truck, a meeting, a stash). The caller is Marjorie Kell (reveal in part 4).
pieces.reward: Story intel; corroboration evidence route for Branch B
pieces.mobile: Calls are subtitled; tips are marked on the minimap only after you check them.

pieces.title: Old Beat Favours
pieces.where: Midtown Central; the old foot posts
pieces.hook: Kearney asks for things he can't do in uniform.
pieces.twist: Small off-book favours (find a missing ledger page, sit with a dying informant, return a kid's bike to the right stoop) that build the 'Old Beat' special.

pieces.title: Getting Licensed
pieces.where: Taxi bureau (invented), Kehoe's office, a doctor, a photo booth
pieces.hook: Teddy wants his hack licence back. The city wants seven forms.
pieces.twist: A comic bureaucracy crawl across the small map: each office needs something from another. Shortcut with a bribe, or do it straight and earn Kehoe's respect.
pieces.mobile: Each step is a short walk.

pieces.title: The Club's Emergencies
pieces.hook: A member's rent is due, a member's son (adult) is in the Tombs, a member's landlord changed the lock.
pieces.twist: Each emergency uses a different system (bail, keys, a bribe, a fight), and how Delphine solves it changes the club's vote in M31.

pieces.title: The Practice Chair
pieces.hook: Tina wants to learn hair. A barber lets them practise after hours.
pieces.twist: A gentle rhythm game (cut, wash, set) with regulars who talk. A rest from the violence; it pays off the shop dream.
pieces.reward: Tina +1; the epilogue shop's first customers

pieces.title: Rent Day
pieces.where: Nick's properties (the W 29th building, W 37th storefront, the Corwin)
pieces.hook: Rent day at Nick's buildings never goes smoothly.
pieces.twist: Trouble events (a burst pipe, a tenant strike, a cop's hand out) where Nick can spend, listen, or fight badly, and each choice shows up in the Corwin's fate.

pieces.title: The Buyers' Banquet
pieces.hook: Nick hosts out-of-town buyers; Kallis sabotages.
pieces.twist: A social stealth puzzle: keep buyers happy at the right table while finding Kallis's man spiking the champagne.

pieces.title: Nick Can't Sleep
pieces.hook: Nick drives at night when he can't sleep.
pieces.twist: Map discovery as character: each drive reveals a hidden place (an after-hours club, a garage, a rooftop bar) through a memory Nick tells aloud.
pieces.reward: Hidden places unlocked on the minimap

pieces.title: The Projectionist's Reels
pieces.where: Cinemas, pawnshops and alleys on the Deuce
pieces.hook: A projectionist lost reels of a 1940s New York picture across the Deuce.
pieces.twist: Find 12 reels; each restores a scene. With all 12, the Velvet Moon holds a midnight screening of an invented lost film shot on these very streets.
pieces.reward: A screening cutscene; the film's poster for a lead's home

pieces.title: Behind the Passage Gate
pieces.hook: Teddy's keys open a shuttered gate in the old passage.
pieces.twist: Forgotten shopfronts from the 1940s: a shoeshine stand's last customer list, a florist's frozen calendar. A quiet exploration with rats, and a cache of period cash.

pieces.title: Last Train Home
pieces.hook: A tipsy office worker (adult) asks you to get her home on the last train.
pieces.twist: Escort through stations, transfers and a stalled train in a tunnel. Rats, a sermon, a three-piece band. Get off at the right stop.
pieces.reward: Her thanks and a business card (a future job)

pieces.title: RIZO 147
pieces.where: Subway cars, the passage, a rooftop
pieces.hook: A graffiti writer wants his best piece photographed before the Transit Authority buffs it.
pieces.twist: Find his whole-car piece on a moving train by timing station arrivals, photograph it, and protect his sketchbook from a rival crew. It's about art, not vandalism glamour.
pieces.reward: His piece on the Ticker's front page; a tag on a lead's home wall
pieces.mobile: Train times on the HUD; auto-frame.

pieces.title: The Water-Tank Voice
pieces.where: A rooftop water tank near W 36th St & 9th Ave
pieces.hook: Someone is living in a rooftop water tank, and leaving clues about the block on chalked rooftops.
pieces.twist: A rooftop clue hunt across the walk-ups: read the chalk, climb the right stairwell, find the man in the tank and hear what he's seen from up there. (Reframed 26 Nov: no radio-station content, per the user.)
pieces.reward: A hidden rooftop place unlocked on the minimap
pieces.mobile: Clues are large chalk marks; stairwells are enterable.

pieces.title: Leg Bands
pieces.hook: The Commodore's lost birds still wear his bands.
pieces.twist: Photograph 15 banded pigeons (ambient flocks); each band leads back to a part of his story.
pieces.mobile: Bands are highlighted when the camera is up.

pieces.title: The Posters of '71
pieces.hook: Old wanted posters from 1971 are still pinned up.
pieces.twist: Collect 8. Together they show who was on the street the night of Mayhew's meet, adding lore to M25.
pieces.reward: Lore; a hidden line in M25

pieces.title: Marquee Letters
pieces.hook: Someone stole the Velvet Moon's marquee letters.
pieces.twist: Find 20 letters; the owner spells a message on the marquee chosen by you (from a list), visible for the rest of the game.
pieces.reward: A marquee message of your choice

pieces.title: The Club's Last IOUs
pieces.where: Bus terminal lockers, a church, a train station
pieces.hook: Women who left the city left IOUs with the club.
pieces.twist: Find their last addresses and send their savings home by money order. Bittersweet, and it changes the club's vote.

pieces.title: Fire-Escape Gardens
pieces.hook: Tomato plants on fire escapes all over the West Side.
pieces.twist: Photograph 15. Moretti pays for the best, and the last belongs to Carmen.
pieces.reward: Moretti flowers for the march; Carmen +1

pieces.title: Marked Money
pieces.hook: Calloway marks some bills to trace the pad.
pieces.twist: Collection rounds with a twist: decide which envelopes carry marked bills (if Teddy wore the wire) or spot them (if he burned it). The stops are moral scenes, not a pickup route.

pieces.title: Night Desk Requests
pieces.hook: Residents ring the desk bell at night.
pieces.twist: Two-block errands that build relationship gates; in Act 3 they become organising tasks.

pieces.title: Brownout Relief
pieces.hook: Dark blocks need ice, candles and a hand.
pieces.twist: Navigate by lit landmarks only; looters (combat) or bribes.
